sections.title: Introduction to the Gospel
observations: Paul introduces himself as a servant of Christ, emphasizing his apostolic authority and mission to spread the Gospel.
The Gospel is described as the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, highlighting its universal offer and transformative nature.

sections.title: The Righteousness of God Revealed
observations: Paul explains that in the Gospel, the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith, indicating that faith is both the means and the result of salvation.
This section emphasizes the importance of faith in the believer's life and the necessity of living by faith.

sections.title: God's Wrath Against Sin
observations: Paul discusses the wrath of God being revealed against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, indicating that God's judgment is a response to human sin.
He outlines the consequences of rejecting God, including a darkened mind and moral decay, which serves as a warning to the readers.

importantVerses.commentary: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith; as it is written, 'The righteous shall live by faith.'

questions: What does Paul mean by the 'power of God for salvation'?
How does the concept of righteousness in Romans differ from other biblical texts?
What implications does the revelation of God's wrath have for contemporary believers?
In what ways can we see the theme of faith being central to the message of Romans?
